top_violation_types.title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A sampling of children records were evaluated. One child's immunization record was observed incomplete.

top_violation_types.title: Requirement of Gas Leak Inspection (26 TAC §746.5401)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not have a current gas inspection on file.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it has been determined that a child was left unattended, the caregiver was not at a physical proximity that allowed visual and/or auditory awareness of the child in care.

top_violation_types.title: Requirements for Infants - Prompt Attention to Needs (26 TAC §742.501(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the DFPS investigation, the caregiver did not give proper attention to physical needs of the child as the caregiver propped a bottle for a four-month-old infant and then walked away without providing adequate supervision.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §742.303(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: It has been determined through interviews, that the older children in care did change diapers of the younger children and had clean up duties.

top_violation_types.title: Healthy Environment - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §742.801(d))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The backyard where children play had an axe and a hammer where children could access it and was reported to be out at all times. The yard also had several tools and machines that pose a safety risk to children in care.

top_violation_types.title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - installed and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions (26 TAC §746.5625(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The electronic child safety alarm was observed not functioning in one of the operation's vans used to transport the children in care.

top_violation_types.title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One food allergy plan was not signed by the parent.
